lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | May 2023 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Delete the date of birth.
items.because: It is not relevant to hiring and can create unnecessary age-discrimination or privacy concerns.

items.says: Remove nationality unless a specific application requires it.
items.because: Nationality is generally not useful on a North American technical resume.

items.says: Check whether the portfolio URL is useful.
items.because: A link creates an expectation that the reviewer can quickly verify your projects.

items.says: Add a professional title or summary beneath your contact information.
items.because: A recruiter currently has to infer your target role from the bullets.

items.says: Consider adding one compact line of relevant coursework, research, or specialization only if it directly supports ML systems, deep learning, distributed systems, or LLM work.
items.because: The degree is current and relevant, but the resume gives no indication of what your graduate specialization contributes to your target role.

items.says: Make the expected status visually clear and ensure the date does not look like a completed degree.
items.because: Recruiters may otherwise misread the degree as completed.

items.says: Add academic distinction, honors, or a relevant capstone only if it is genuinely strong.
items.because: Additional detail is only worthwhile if it improves your technical positioning.

items.says: Specify the evaluation context more clearly: what 'accuracy' means, what the comparison baseline was, and whether the result came from a held-out or production-validated set.
items.because: A 35% improvement is compelling, but 'diagnostic accuracy' can mean absolute percentage points, relative improvement, or a particular classification metric.

items.says: Explain or simplify the phrase describing validated tool-use trajectories and assistant-only loss masking if space permits.
items.because: It is technically interesting but dense.

items.says: Clarify the operational purpose of the routing layer and the meaning of 'reviewer disagreement.'
items.because: The reduction from 14% to 6% is strong, but the reader needs to understand what 'disagreement' means.

items.says: Make the relationship between the three specialists, the reviewer, and the input signals easier to understand.
items.because: The architecture is a differentiator, but the current phrasing requires the reader to reconstruct the system design.

items.says: Add the evaluation conditions that make the comparison credible, especially dataset or case count, whether accuracy was statistically comparable, and whether the latency result was measured in production or offline.
items.because: This is highly relevant to current agent-engineering roles.

items.says: Avoid presenting GRPO as the main achievement unless the results are clearly tied to system-level value.
items.because: Recruiters may treat algorithm names as buzzwords.

items.says: Add the consequence of catching the two regressions if you can substantiate it—for example, whether they were prevented from reaching release or production.
items.because: Evaluation infrastructure is valuable, but the current bullet stops just before the business or engineering impact.

items.says: Identify whether you owned the harness, designed the evaluation methodology, or implemented part of a larger system.
items.because: The ownership level matters, especially because the rest of the resume uses strong ownership language.

items.says: Remove this bullet from this position, or merge its distinct contribution into the earlier fine-tuning bullet.
items.because: It repeats the technical method already mentioned in the first bullet without adding a new outcome.

items.says: If the second bullet represents a genuinely separate experiment, explain the separate result rather than repeating the method.
items.because: Methods without a distinct result are weaker than achievements with measurable impact.

items.says: Keep this bullet only if it is genuinely separate from the backlog-reduction bullet in the Research-Agent Evaluation Framework project.
items.because: The project section contains nearly the same achievement.

items.says: If this is the same work, keep it in only one location—probably Experience—and remove the duplicate from Projects.
items.because: Production work should generally receive more prominence than a project entry.

items.says: Explain what the 68% reduction is measured against and over what period.
items.because: The baseline and operational significance should be unambiguous.

items.says: Add the practical consequence if available: larger model or batch size, fewer out-of-memory failures, lower infrastructure cost, or faster training.
items.because: A fourfold memory reduction is impressive, but the reader needs to know what it enabled.

items.says: Clarify whether the 4x figure refers to peak GPU memory, allocated memory, or another measurement.
items.because: Precise technical metrics improve credibility with technical reviewers.

items.says: Clarify whether the p95 values were measured under the same workload and traffic conditions.
items.because: Latency comparisons are only meaningful when the load and test conditions are comparable.

items.says: Make sure the build-failure safeguard was actually enforced in CI rather than merely documented.
items.because: The safeguard is a strong reliability signal if it was automated and routinely used.

items.says: Correct the grammar and tense inconsistency in the phrase describing what the pipeline does.
items.because: The current wording shifts from past tense to present-tense third-person wording and reads like an editing error.

items.says: Clarify what 'release cycles to 3 days' means—three days from code completion to release, or a reduction to a three-day cycle.
items.because: The current phrasing is ambiguous and may be interpreted differently by different readers.

items.says: Quantify the prior cycle length or the number of releases if available.
items.because: The impact is difficult to assess without a baseline.

items.says: State the operational result more precisely if possible: fewer failed jobs, elimination of a recurring backlog, improved dispatch reliability, or reduced manual intervention.
items.because: The outcome should show why the architecture mattered.

items.says: Clarify your ownership of the migration across 30 services.
items.because: Make sure the wording accurately reflects whether you led it, implemented it, or contributed to a larger team effort.

items.says: Fix the line-break artifact in 'dead-letter handling.'
items.because: Hyphenation caused by PDF or source formatting should not appear as an awkward split in the final document.

items.says: Remove this bullet or replace it with a concrete technical or adoption metric.
items.because: 'Drove adoption,' 'AI-first,' 'accelerating delivery,' and 'improving outcomes' are all broad claims without evidence.

items.says: If there is no measurable adoption or engineering outcome, omit the bullet.
items.because: A vague leadership claim lowers the quality of the section.

items.says: Explain the constraint and comparison more clearly.
items.because: The 100-turn test and context limit are interesting, but 'raw conversation grew 100x' is difficult to interpret.

items.says: State what the context-management design enabled—cost control, stable latency, successful task completion, or avoidance of context-window failure.
items.because: The implementation technique matters less than the resulting system behavior.

items.says: Make sure the stress test is representative enough to support the claim.
items.because: A technical reviewer may ask whether the test used realistic tool calls, message sizes, and workloads.

items.says: Add the conditions under which the deadlocks and lost results occurred, if that can be done concisely.
items.because: This is a strong systems bullet because it demonstrates diagnosis and resolution of concurrency failures.

items.says: Clarify whether '50-way fan-out' was a tested upper bound, production workload, or stress-test configuration.
items.because: The number is useful, but its meaning depends on context.

items.says: Identify the effect on reliability or throughput if measured.
items.because: Demonstrating improved successful completion or throughput would make the result more compelling.

items.says: Identify the nature of the contribution: implementation, metric adaptation, test coverage, API design, or integration into the framework.
items.because: A technical reviewer will want to know what you actually built.

items.says: Include the public repository or project link if it is genuinely open source and accessible.
items.because: Open-source contribution is a credibility signal only when reviewers can verify it.

items.says: Add what the correlation means operationally—for example, whether the evaluator correctly ranked degraded outputs or detected quality loss.
items.because: Many readers will not immediately understand what a Kendall correlation of 0.89 demonstrates.

items.says: Clarify the unit of analysis and the source of the 400+ trials if possible.
items.because: The reviewer may want to know whether these were synthetic, human-authored, or production-like reports.

items.says: Remove this bullet from the project unless the project truly produced this result independently.
items.because: It duplicates the Mobility Systems Company achievement in wording, inputs, and outcome.

items.says: If this was a separate contribution, distinguish it through different ownership, data, evaluation setting, or result.
items.because: Otherwise, the resume appears to count one accomplishment twice.

items.says: Keep only tools you can use comfortably in an interview or practical assessment.
items.because: The list is credible but short. That is preferable to including technologies you cannot defend.

items.says: Consider separating languages from development tools if you add more substantiated skills.
items.because: Programming languages, version control, and infrastructure tools signal different capabilities.

items.says: Add only technologies clearly demonstrated elsewhere in the resume, such as model fine-tuning, tool-use systems, inference optimization, evaluation harnesses, or distributed systems.
items.because: The current skills section does not fully capture the strongest technical themes already present in the experience.

items.says: Avoid adding broad labels such as 'AI,' 'machine learning,' or 'LLMs' without supporting specifics.
items.because: Broad labels add little value and can make the skills section look generic.

items.says: Consider adding testing, CI/CD, APIs, caching, queues, or GPU optimization only if you can discuss the implementation details.
items.because: These are real strengths shown in your bullets, but they should not become a keyword list detached from evidence.

items.says: Order the most relevant bullets first within each role.
items.because: Recruiters often read only the first bullet or two under each position.

items.says: Decide whether the primary story is ML/LLM engineering, agent infrastructure, applied research/evaluation, or general software engineering for ML systems.
items.because: The resume currently supports all four interpretations. That breadth is useful, but without prioritization it may make your target unclear.

items.says: Remove duplicated claims: assistant-only loss masking appears twice; diagnostics triage/backlog reduction appears in both Experience and Projects.
items.because: Duplicate content reduces perceived breadth and can raise questions about whether metrics are being counted more than once.
